title: Daily News Quiz · 2026-09-07
headline: LUX-ZEPLIN detector records one high-energy flash that could be dark matter

questions.prompt: Who presented the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy result at the Tendo conference?
choices: Samuel Eriksen of the University of Bristol
questions.hintKo: The presenter was a particle physicist on the LZ team, not a chef or designer.

questions.prompt: What material fills the LUX-ZEPLIN detector that recorded the flash?
questions.hintKo: The tank holds xenon, not food or fuel.

questions.prompt: When did the team analyse observational data for this search?
choices: From March twenty twenty-three to April twenty twenty-four
questions.hintKo: The data window was in twenty twenty-three and twenty twenty-four, not a holiday.

questions.prompt: Where is the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment located?
choices: Lead, South Dakota, at the Sanford Underground Research Facility
questions.hintKo: The experiment is underground in South Dakota, not on the moon.

questions.prompt: Why are researchers cautious about calling the flash a dark-matter discovery?
choices: The flash was caused by a phone camera
They already proved dark matter last week
Previous hopeful signals turned out to be spurious and they need more data
questions.hintKo: Caution comes from history and the need for replication, not missing equipment.

questions.prompt: How much energy did the single leftover recoil deposit in the detector?
questions.hintKo: The measured energy was two hundred forty-eight kiloelectronvolts, not money or weight.
